_disclaimer: This file contains entirely fabricated, illustrative audience segment data created for demonstration and development purposes only. It does not represent real Seven West Media, LiSTNR, Hit Network, Triple M, The West Australian, PerthNow, The Nightly, or 7NEWS.com.au inventory, actual audience sizes, genuine CPM rates, or any proprietary data. All figures — reach, index, CPM, identity match rates — are invented for realism and must not be quoted, shared, or relied upon as factual. All named brands are real media properties; this taxonomy is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or derived from any official product.

segments.description: Adults watching Seven News at 6pm across the Seven Network in Australian metro and regional markets; the largest single-night news audience on Australian free-to-air television, reaching a broad cross-section of Australians aged 35 to 70+ who prioritise live, trusted news as part of their evening routine. Linear contextual buy — not individually addressable.
segments.notes: Linear broadcast buy — audience is contextual, not individually targeted. Strong household-decision-maker skew. Overlaps heavily with SEV_BVD_001 (7plus catch-up) and SEV_DIG_001 (7NEWS digital) — stacking all three over-indexes against news-engaged audiences. Book 4-6 weeks in advance for peak news periods (election cycles, major sporting events).

segments.description: Viewers of AFL matches, AFL Footy Show coverage, and AFL news segments broadcast on Seven Network and 7mate during prime time and weekend windows; skews male 25-54 with a strong regional Australian component, particularly WA (West Coast Eagles, Fremantle Dockers) and Victoria. One of the highest-rating sports properties on Australian free-to-air television.
segments.notes: SEASONAL — AFL season runs March to September; Grand Final week (late September) commands significant CPM premium (add 40-60% to indicative range). Strong WA skew for West Coast Eagles and Fremantle Dockers fixtures. Cross-media AFL audience is best reached by stacking with SEV_BVD_002 and SEV_AUD_002. Linear contextual only — no individual addressability.

segments.description: Viewers of Sunrise, Australia's most-watched breakfast television program on Seven Network, tuning in weekday mornings for news, weather, lifestyle segments, and celebrity interviews; predominantly women aged 35-65 with a stay-at-home, retired, or shift-worker demographic skew. High brand affinity environment — Sunrise viewers demonstrate strong sponsor recall.
segments.notes: High-loyalty morning viewing habit — Sunrise viewers show strong weekly return rates. Overlaps with SEV_AUD_001 (breakfast radio) for morning routine consumers. Women 35-65 household decision-makers make this an effective environment for supermarket, healthcare, insurance, and travel brands. Linear contextual — not individually addressable.

segments.description: Viewers of home renovation, gardening, cooking, and lifestyle programs broadcast across Seven Network and 7two, including Better Homes & Gardens TV, renovation specials, and lifestyle magazine programs; predominantly women 30-60 engaged with domestic decision-making content including homewares, renovations, and garden design. One of Australian television's most commercially responsive lifestyle audiences.
segments.notes: Reliable Saturday night and weekend daytime audience. Strong cross-over with SEV_BVD_005 (7plus home lifestyle streamers) and SEV_PUB_006 (PerthNow lifestyle) for extended home and lifestyle reach package. Seasonality peaks spring (renovation planning) and autumn (indoor nesting). Linear contextual only.

segments.description: Viewers of true crime documentaries, investigative journalism programs, and factual drama broadcast on Seven Network and 7plus primetime; a growing audience segment driven by the mainstream breakout of true crime content in Australian television, skewing female 28-55 with high completion rates and strong social media sharing behaviour around program content.
segments.notes: Cross-media true crime audience — stack with SEV_BVD_004 (7plus true crime) and SEV_AUD_003 (LiSTNR true crime podcast) for full-funnel coverage across broadcast, streaming, and audio. Female 28-55 skew makes this an effective environment for insurance, legal services, security products, and investigative-aligned brand messaging.

segments.description: Viewers of 7Bravo's curated programming schedule of US reality, lifestyle, and entertainment content targeted at women 18-49; including Real Housewives franchise, Below Deck, and similar aspirational lifestyle programming that delivers a younger, more engaged female audience than Seven Network's broader news and sport schedule.
segments.notes: Younger female skew distinguishes 7Bravo from broader Seven Network buys. Effective for fashion, beauty, travel, food, and entertainment brands targeting aspirational women 18-44. Overlaps ~30% with SEV_BVD_007 (7plus young women's entertainment). Linear contextual only.

segments.description: Male-skewed audience watching 7mate's sports, action, and entertainment programming including motorsport, combat sports, US NFL broadcasts, and action movie marathons; core male 20-50 audience with demonstrated interest in sport, vehicles, technology, and outdoor activities.
segments.notes: Complements SEV_AUD_002 (Triple M sports) for a broadcast-plus-audio sports audience package. Strong for auto, beer, insurance, and hardware brands. Linear contextual only. AFL season delivers a significant reach uplift during 7mate simulcast matches.

segments.description: Viewers of 7flix's film, series, and entertainment programming including movie premiers, classic series, and entertainment specials; a broad reach audience watching in relaxed, high-attention viewing environments, with an even gender split and a skew toward 30-65 adults in multi-person households.
segments.notes: Broad reach extension channel at efficient CPM. Useful as frequency-building layer in a multi-channel Seven Network plan. Weekend movie timeslots deliver highest viewership. Linear contextual only.

segments.description: Viewers of 7two's classic entertainment, family programming, and long-running drama series; skews older (55+) with strong regional and suburban viewership, representing Australians who value familiar, comfortable viewing and demonstrate consistent appointment television habits.
segments.notes: Strong 55+ skew. Efficient CPM for mass reach brands targeting mature Australians — health insurance, banking, pharmaceutical, funeral planning, and travel. Linear contextual only.

segments.segment_name: Seven Network Prime Time — Total Network
segments.description: Unduplicated total reach across all Seven Network channels (Seven, 7two, 7mate, 7flix, 7Bravo) during prime time (6pm–10:30pm); the broadest possible linear television reach package in the Seven portfolio, suitable for mass-market brand building campaigns where demographic precision is less important than raw reach and brand-safe contextual alignment.
segments.notes: Highest reach segment in the portfolio. Suitable for FMCG, telco, supermarket, and financial services brands requiring national mass coverage. Linear contextual — no individual targeting. Effective as the broadcast anchor for a cross-media package where digital and audio add precision on top of television reach.

segments.description: 7plus registered users who regularly stream Seven News, Sunrise, and current affairs catch-up content on-demand; individually addressable through 7plus's registered user base, allowing demographic and behavioural targeting layered on top of news content context. More addressable and measurable than linear broadcast equivalent.
segments.notes: Addressable via 7plus registered user data — high identity match rate enables frequency management and audience extension to digital. Overlaps strongly with SEV_BTV_001 (linear Seven News) — plan deduplication when stacking. BVOD delivers completion rates 70-85% versus linear; effective for brand messaging requiring message delivery.

segments.description: 7plus registered users streaming AFL matches live and on-demand via the 7plus platform, including live game streams, AFL Highlights packages, and press conference catch-up; addressable AFL audience extending the broadcast AFL buy into digital video with registered user targeting and cross-device frequency management.
segments.notes: SEASONAL — AFL season March to September. Completes the AFL cross-media package alongside SEV_BTV_002 (linear AFL) and SEV_AUD_002 (Triple M). WA-specific AFL content (Eagles, Dockers) available as sub-targeting option. 7plus AFL streamers index strongly for 25-44 males, extending into a demographic underrepresented in linear AFL buys.

segments.description: 7plus users demonstrating high-session streaming behaviour across drama series, mini-series, and event television; characterised by multiple consecutive episode views, series completion, and return streaming within 7 days of new episode availability. Highly engaged viewing environment with above-average ad completion and recall.
segments.notes: High-engagement streaming audience — binge behaviour correlates with high ad completion rates (80%+). Skews female 25-50. Addressable via 7plus registration. Series sponsorship and branded content integration available alongside standard pre-roll. No strong seasonal pattern — driven by program slate releases.

segments.description: 7plus users streaming true crime documentaries, investigative features, and factual programming on-demand; a high-loyalty streaming audience who seek out true crime content specifically, often completing full series and returning for new content within days of availability. Extends the broadcast true crime audience into an individually addressable BVOD environment.
segments.notes: Cross-media true crime package: stack with SEV_BTV_005 (broadcast true crime) and SEV_AUD_003 (LiSTNR true crime podcast) for full-funnel reach. High female 28-50 skew. Addressable streaming environment allows demographic refinement and frequency capping.

segments.description: 7plus users streaming home renovation, cooking, and lifestyle programming on-demand, including Better Homes & Gardens episodes, renovation specials, and lifestyle magazine programs; extends the broadcast home and lifestyle audience into a targeted, individually addressable BVOD context with demographic refinement capabilities.
segments.notes: Addressable extension of SEV_BTV_004 (broadcast home lifestyle). Stack with SEV_DIG_006 (display home researchers) and SEV_PUB_006 (PerthNow lifestyle) for a full home and lifestyle cross-media package. Spring activation peak. Women 30-60 household decision-maker skew.

segments.description: 7plus registered female users aged 18-35 streaming entertainment, drama, reality, and lifestyle content; a younger female demographic underrepresented in linear television who consume Seven content primarily or exclusively through streaming. High mobile and connected-TV streaming via 7plus app, characterised by evening and weekend viewing sessions.
segments.notes: Strongest younger female demographic in the Seven portfolio. Valuable for beauty, fashion, food delivery, financial services, and entertainment brands targeting Gen Z and younger Millennials. Addressable via 7plus registration enables precise age and gender targeting.

segments.description: 7plus users streaming Sunrise and morning news catch-up content during morning commute, breakfast, and early work-day windows; extends the morning routine broadcast audience into an addressable streaming context, reaching Australians consuming morning media on mobile and tablet devices.
segments.notes: Morning routine audience. Complements SEV_AUD_001 (Hit Network breakfast) for cross-media morning reach package. Mobile-heavy consumption — optimise creative for mobile completion. Overlaps with SEV_BTV_003 (Sunrise linear) — plan deduplication.

segments.description: Listeners of the Hit Network breakfast shows across capital city stations during 6am-9am weekday windows; a broad, younger-skewing radio audience (18-44) engaged with entertainment, pop music, and lifestyle conversation content during their morning commute and household routine. Hit breakfast shows consistently rank among the top-rating breakfast programs in their respective markets.
segments.notes: Linear radio — contextual only, not individually addressable. Morning commute environment; short-form creative (15 seconds) outperforms 30-second spots in this daypart. Cross-media morning package available by stacking with SEV_BTV_003 (Sunrise) and SEV_BVD_007 (7plus morning). 18-44 skew; effective for FMCG, fast food, entertainment, and retail.

segments.segment_name: Triple M Footy & Sports Show Listeners
segments.description: Triple M listeners across AFL Footy Show programs, weekend live AFL call, Triple M Sports Riff, and sports news programming; predominantly male 25-54 sports fans with strong AFL team loyalty, engaging with sports talk radio in drive-time and weekend dayparts. Triple M's AFL coverage creates one of Australian radio's most loyal and commercially engaged sports audiences.
segments.notes: SEASONAL boost — AFL season March to September adds 20-30% reach uplift. Core AFL cross-media audience: stack with SEV_BTV_002 (Seven AFL broadcast) and SEV_BVD_002 (7plus AFL) for full cross-media AFL package. Male 25-54 skew. Beer, betting, auto, and sports retail brands deliver strong recall in Triple M sports context. Linear radio — contextual only.

segments.description: Listeners of LiSTNR's true crime podcast slate, including Australian true crime originals, cold case investigations, and forensic storytelling programs; a highly engaged, deliberate-listening audience who seek out true crime content specifically, listening in full and sharing episodes actively. Among the fastest-growing podcast categories on the LiSTNR platform.
segments.notes: Podcast placement — individually addressable through LiSTNR registration data. Full cross-media true crime package: stack with SEV_BTV_005 (broadcast) and SEV_BVD_004 (BVOD). Host-read and branded content integration available at premium. Female 28-50 skew. High listener completion and brand recall rates typical of true crime podcast environments.

segments.description: Hit Network afternoon drive-time listeners (3pm-7pm weekdays) across capital city markets, tuning in during post-work commute and after-school pickup routines; a broad 25-50 mixed audience engaging with pop hits, entertainment news, and light lifestyle conversation at the day's highest radio listening peak.
segments.notes: Drive-time is the highest-reach radio daypart. Broad 25-50 audience; efficient mass reach for retail, FMCG, supermarket, and fast food brands. Linear radio — contextual only. Friday drive-time delivers highest Friday-weekend purchase intent priming.

segments.description: Triple M listeners engaging with classic rock, contemporary hits, and comedy programming outside AFL/sport dayparts; a broad male-skewing 30-55 audience with strong regional Australian representation, engaging with Triple M's personality-driven, irreverent programming during morning, daytime, and evening shifts.
segments.notes: Broad male 30-55 audience. Strong regional reach. Effective for hardware, automotive, beer, and sports retail brands. Linear radio — contextual only. Can be combined with SEV_AUD_002 (Triple M Sports) for full Triple M network buy.

segments.segment_name: LiSTNR News & Current Affairs Podcast Listeners
segments.description: LiSTNR subscribers engaging with daily news briefings, political commentary podcasts, and current affairs deep-dives on the LiSTNR platform; a news-engaged, higher-education audience consuming informed audio content during morning routines, gym sessions, and commutes — individually addressable through LiSTNR's registered subscriber base.
segments.notes: Addressable podcast audience via LiSTNR registration. Higher education and income skew. Morning consumption pattern overlaps with SEV_BTV_003 (Sunrise) and SEV_AUD_001 (Hit breakfast) for extended morning news package. Effective for financial services, premium brands, health insurance, and news-adjacent advertisers.

segments.description: LiSTNR listeners engaging with personal finance, investing, entrepreneurship, and business podcasts on the platform; an older, higher-income, educated audience consuming financial content during commutes and exercise sessions, individually addressable through LiSTNR's registered user data and demonstrating high affinity with financial services advertising.
segments.notes: Highest-index audio segment in the finance category. Addressable via LiSTNR registration. AFSL compliance required for investment product advertising. Stack with SEV_PUB_005 (The West Business) and SEV_DIG_005 (7NEWS finance digital) for a full cross-media finance-engaged audience. EOFY window (May-Jun) delivers strongest engagement.

segments.description: Hit Network weekend listeners during Saturday and Sunday daytime programming, engaging with entertainment countdown shows, celebrity interviews, and light weekend lifestyle content; a relaxed, leisure-mode audience with higher dwell time than weekday commute listening, effective for weekend retail, entertainment, and experience brands.
segments.notes: Weekend leisure audience. Higher dwell time than weekday. Effective for weekend retail, restaurant, entertainment venue, and experience brands wanting to reach Australians in planning mode for weekend activities. Linear radio — contextual only.

segments.segment_name: The West Australian Daily Print & Digital Readers
segments.description: Subscribers and regular readers of The West Australian — WA's dominant daily newspaper — consuming news, opinion, business, and sport coverage across print and digital platforms; a predominantly WA-resident audience representing the most loyal and influential news readership in Western Australia, with strong decision-maker, business owner, and community leader representation.
segments.notes: WA-specific audience — highest geographic concentration in the portfolio. Strong community leadership, business owner, and decision-maker skew. Addressable via subscriber data. The West Australian holds a dominant position in WA daily news; reaching this audience is essential for WA market campaigns. Overlaps ~55% with SEV_PUB_002 (PerthNow) — plan deduplication when stacking.

segments.description: Regular readers of PerthNow, WA's most-visited free digital news site, browsing breaking news, community stories, sport, entertainment, and WA lifestyle content; a broader, younger WA digital audience than The West Australian's subscriber base, with strong mobile consumption and high return-visit frequency driven by WA-specific news alerts and local community stories.
segments.notes: Largest free digital WA news reach in the portfolio. Younger and more mobile-heavy than The West Australian. Strong for WA retail, property, entertainment, and services brands requiring local market coverage. Overlaps ~55% with SEV_PUB_001 (The West) — treat as younger, broader WA reach extension rather than a separate buy.

segments.segment_name: The Nightly National Politics & Opinion Readers
segments.description: Subscribers and regular readers of The Nightly, the Seven West Media national digital newspaper covering politics, opinion, international affairs, and analysis; an engaged, higher-education, news-literate audience seeking quality long-form journalism and opinion beyond the daily news cycle. The Nightly reader skews professional, 30-65, with above-average income and political engagement.
segments.notes: Highest-index publishing segment in the portfolio. Small but highly engaged, educated, and influential readership. Effective for financial services, premium consumer brands, professional services, and policy-adjacent advertisers. Addressable via subscriber data. Newsletter activation delivers strong open rates (35-42% average). National audience — not WA-limited despite being a Seven West Media property.

segments.description: Regular readers of 7NEWS.com.au consuming national and international breaking news, politics, crime, and human interest stories; the digital news complement to Seven Network's television news, reaching Australians who consume news primarily or additionally through digital publishing alongside or instead of the linear broadcast. Broad national audience with strong return-visit frequency.
segments.notes: Largest publishing reach segment in the portfolio. Broad national audience. Overlaps with SEV_BTV_001 (linear Seven News) and SEV_BVD_001 (7plus news) — the three together form a full news cross-media package. Addressable digital placement. Effective for broad-market advertisers wanting news-aligned brand safety context at scale.

segments.segment_name: The West Australian Business & Finance Readers
segments.description: The West Australian readers engaging specifically with Business, Finance, Mining & Resources, Property, and WA Economy coverage; WA's primary business news audience, including mining executives, small business owners, property investors, and finance professionals whose primary business news source is The West Australian. Strong WA decision-maker concentration.
segments.notes: WA business decision-maker audience. High CPM justified by executive and owner skew. AFSL compliance required for investment and financial product advertising. Mining and resources industry representation is unique to The West Australian versus national business publications. Stack with SEV_AUD_007 (LiSTNR finance podcast) for WA business cross-media package.

segments.description: PerthNow readers engaging with lifestyle, entertainment, food, and community content sections; a broader, younger WA audience interested in local events, restaurant reviews, entertainment news, and community lifestyle content. High mobile consumption and social sharing behaviour characteristic of digitally-native WA content consumers aged 20-45.
segments.notes: WA lifestyle audience — complementary to The West Australian for a full WA digital publishing package. Younger demographic (20-45) with high mobile consumption. Effective for WA hospitality, entertainment, retail, and local services brands. Overlaps ~35% with SEV_PUB_001 (The West) — use for WA reach extension into younger demographics.

segments.description: 7NEWS.com.au readers engaging specifically with the Sport section, consuming AFL match reports, cricket, tennis, rugby league, and general sport news; a male-skewing sports digital audience that extends the broadcast AFL and sports audience into a contextual digital publishing environment with programmatic display activation capability.
segments.notes: Digital sports audience extending broadcast and audio sports package. Addressable via display. Complements SEV_BTV_002 (AFL broadcast) and SEV_AUD_002 (Triple M sports). SEASONAL boost during AFL and cricket seasons. Male 25-54 skew.

segments.segment_name: The West Australian Real Estate & Property Readers
segments.description: The West Australian readers engaging with Real Estate section, property market commentary, suburb profiles, new development features, and WA-specific housing market analysis; a WA property audience with strong in-market purchase and investment intent, representing buyers, sellers, investors, and property industry professionals operating in the WA residential and commercial market.
segments.notes: WA property market audience. Saturday Real Estate section is the most-read section of The West Australian. AFSL/credit compliance for mortgage and finance product advertising. WA-specific property market dynamics — monitor RBA rate decisions. Effective for WA real estate agencies, mortgage brokers, builders, and property platforms.

segments.segment_name: The Nightly Arts, Culture & Weekend Reads
segments.description: The Nightly subscribers engaging with arts, culture, film, book reviews, travel, and long-form weekend magazine features; a culturally engaged, higher-education, 35-65 audience who value quality journalism and cultural commentary. Strong newsletter open rates and sustained page depth distinguishing this from casual news browsing.
segments.notes: Small but high-value cultural audience. Newsletter is the primary activation — The Nightly Weekend newsletter achieves 38% average open rate. Effective for cultural institutions, premium travel, wine, book publishers, film and arts brands. Addressable via subscriber data.

segments.description: PerthNow readers consuming health, wellness, community services, and wellbeing content including local healthcare news, community event listings, mental health awareness features, and WA-specific health and welfare topics; a community-connected WA audience motivated by local health and wellbeing information.
segments.notes: WA health and community audience. Effective for WA health services, pharmacies, community not-for-profits, and health insurance brands. Sensitive category — pharmaceutical and health product advertising should comply with TGA requirements. Consistent year-round engagement.

segments.description: 7NEWS.com.au and associated digital properties users visiting five or more times per month, demonstrating strong news habit and brand loyalty; individually addressable through programmatic audience activation, with cross-device identity matching enabling frequency management and audience extension across the Seven digital network. The highest-engagement digital news segment in the portfolio.
segments.notes: High-loyalty digital news audience. Addressable. Cross-device identity matching enables frequency management. Overlaps with SEV_BTV_001 (linear news) and SEV_BVD_001 (BVOD news) for full news cross-media package. Strong for brand-safety-conscious advertisers wanting premium news context in a programmatic environment.

segments.description: Contextual display inventory across Seven West Media's WA-focused digital properties including The West Australian online, PerthNow, and 7NEWS WA pages, targeted to Western Australian metro users; the broadest WA digital reach package available through the Seven network, combining news, lifestyle, sport, and entertainment contexts into a single WA geo-targeted buy.
segments.notes: Broadest WA digital reach at lowest CPM in the portfolio. Contextual geo-targeted — not individually addressable. Effective WA market entry point or frequency-extension layer for campaigns with strong WA emphasis. Use addressable segments (SEV_PUB_001, SEV_PUB_002) for precise WA targeting; use this segment for WA reach-maximisation at efficient CPM.

segments.description: Users across Seven's digital properties engaging with AFL news articles, match previews, ladder and statistics pages, and AFL editorial on 7NEWS.com.au and associated digital channels; a digitally-native AFL audience complementing the broadcast and audio AFL buy with addressable digital reach, enabling frequency management and audience extension across the AFL season.
segments.notes: SEASONAL — AFL season March to September. Addressable digital AFL audience extending the broadcast-audio AFL package. Full AFL cross-media: SEV_BTV_002 + SEV_BVD_002 + SEV_AUD_002 + SEV_DIG_003. Enables cross-device frequency capping and audience measurement across the AFL campaign. WA AFL sub-targeting available.

segments.description: Women aged 25-54 engaging with lifestyle, health, entertainment, and home content across Seven's digital network, identified through behavioural signals and cross-site engagement patterns; the portfolio's primary women's digital behavioural segment, enabling addressable targeting of the core female household decision-maker demographic across Seven's full digital footprint.
segments.notes: Core female behavioural segment. Broad lifestyle reach across Seven's digital network. Addressable with identity matching. Complements SEV_BTV_004 (home lifestyle broadcast) and SEV_BVD_005 (7plus home). Effective for household, beauty, food, health, and retail brands targeting female primary shoppers.

segments.description: 7NEWS.com.au and West Australian digital property users demonstrating sustained engagement with finance, business, property, and economic news content; an above-average income, financially engaged audience reading business commentary, ASX updates, property market analysis, and personal finance content across Seven's digital network.
segments.notes: Finance-engaged digital audience. Addressable. AFSL compliance required for investment product advertising. Stack with SEV_PUB_005 (The West Business) and SEV_AUD_007 (LiSTNR finance podcast) for cross-media finance package. EOFY window (May-Jun) and RBA rate decision weeks deliver measurable engagement uplift.

segments.segment_name: Network Display — Home & Property Digital Researchers
segments.description: Digitally identifiable users researching home improvement, property purchase, real estate, and renovation topics across Seven's digital properties; a high-intent home and property audience demonstrating repeated engagement with relevant content categories, enabling addressable targeting of in-market home and property buyers, renovators, and investors.
segments.notes: In-market home and property digital audience. Addressable. Completes the home cross-media package: SEV_BTV_004 + SEV_BVD_005 + SEV_PUB_006 + SEV_DIG_006. Spring activation peak. Effective for real estate platforms, mortgage brokers, hardware retailers, and home improvement brands.

segments.description: 7NEWS.com.au entertainment section readers and users engaging with celebrity news, film and television reviews, music content, and entertainment features across Seven's digital network; a younger-skewing, high-frequency audience demonstrating strong entertainment content loyalty and high social amplification behaviour.
segments.notes: Younger entertainment audience. High social sharing. Extends BVOD entertainment segments into a broader digital display context. Effective for streaming services, music platforms, entertainment venues, gaming, and FMCG brands targeting younger Australians.

segments.description: Users across Seven's digital network demonstrating in-market automotive research behaviour, identified through engagement with motoring news, car review content, and automotive category signals across 7NEWS.com.au and associated digital properties; an addressable, purchase-intent auto audience enabling programmatic activation for new and used vehicle advertisers.
segments.notes: In-market auto audience. Addressable. Male-skewing but increasingly mixed. Effective for new car launches, used vehicle platforms, car finance, insurance, and aftermarket automotive brands. EOFY (Jun) and post-summer (Feb-Mar) new model release cycles drive seasonal uplift.

segments.description: 7NEWS.com.au and Seven network digital users demonstrating travel research and planning intent through engagement with travel news, destination guides, airline content, and accommodation editorial; a purchase-intent travel audience addressable through Seven's digital network, enabling contextual and behavioural targeting for travel category advertisers.
segments.notes: Travel-intent digital audience. Addressable. Seasonal: January (summer holiday planning) and June-July (winter escape and international travel) are peak windows. Effective for airlines, OTAs, hotel groups, cruise lines, and destination marketing organisations.

segments.description: Contextual display inventory across health, wellbeing, fitness, and lifestyle content sections of Seven's digital network; a broad, non-addressable health context buy suitable for health brands requiring brand-safe health content alignment without the identity matching and CPM premium of behavioural health segments.
segments.notes: Broad health contextual buy. Not individually addressable — contextual alignment only. TGA compliance required for therapeutic product advertising. Suitable for health insurance, pharmacy, wellness, and fitness brands seeking scale in a health-aligned environment without behavioural targeting premiums. Use addressable segments for higher-intent health audiences.
